exposure: Cup detachment during vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery (VAVD)
cup detachment during vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery (VAVD)
outcome: Neonatal birth trauma (subgaleal hematoma, subarachnoid hematoma, subdural hematoma, skull fracture, and/or Erb's palsy)
cohort: 1779 women who attempted VAVD in a tertiary hospital between 2012 and 2014
finding: Cup detachment during VAVD is associated with a higher rate of adverse neonatal outcomes, particularly subarachnoid hematoma and composite neonatal birth trauma.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered with cup detachment during vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery had higher rates of subarachnoid hematoma and composite neonatal birth trauma compared to those without cup detachment.
